# F-22 fidelity implementation guide

**Implementation plan:** The [system-by-system overhaul plan](../overhaul/F22-Mod-Overhaul-Plan.html) lists the changes, priorities and dependencies. Detailed findings and evidence remain in this audit.

**Purpose:** Compare the mod’s behavior with documented F-22 behavior, use named aircraft analogues where F-22 details are unknown, and provide a durable guide for implementation. This is a full re-audit of the previous report.

**Revision baselines:** Initial full review 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT; deeper gap analysis 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT; evidence challenges 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT. **223 behavior comparisons**. All 115 original comparisons and all 343 supporting records have review dispositions. Captures contain 556, 565 and 565 text files respectively. These are per-file reads of shared, actively edited source. Each case identifies its capture; aircraft implementation and binaries were not changed by this audit.

## Assessment and meaning of the results

The mod already represents several narrow documented behaviors and many useful aircraft-system abstractions. It also has specific documented F-22 omissions, identifiable differences from selected substitutes, and important areas whose numerical fidelity cannot be determined from public evidence. **There is no defensible whole-aircraft accuracy percentage.** The reference-specific comparison and its evidence boundary are the result.

This revision corrects earlier overclaims. It credits narrow matches, separates genuine differences from deliberate interface choices, and does not treat an unknown F-22 schedule as an error. A working system is not automatically authentic; a different internal implementation can reproduce the documented outward behavior accurately.

**Verification means source/reference review.** Exact cited code locations were checked against captured file hashes. Complete cited passages were read where access allowed; indexed-only/403 sources are identified in the reference ledger. Proposed acceptance cases have not been flown in DCS. No undisclosed radar, engine, flight-control or defensive-system performance is certified.

### Evidence and applicability

1. Use dated F-22 operator, USAF, manufacturer or primary-authored engineering evidence for the particular behavior it establishes. A rescue document establishes emergency equipment functions, not a production performance deck or complete pilot procedure.
2. Where F-22 behavior is unknown, name the Viper/Hornet analogue and make an explicit adoption decision. Their different control rules are alternatives; they are not a combined mandatory F-22 specification.
3. General radar/AESA and flight-physics sources constrain plausible simulation behavior. General crew-alerting guidance supplies optional design ideas. Civil certification guidance is not an F-22 operating rule. Agreement with a principle does not authenticate production coefficients, operating timing or APG-77/F119 curves.
4. Keep unsupported details unresolved or bounded as estimates. A modernization requirement, demonstration or development-era design is not proof of fleet-wide current installation.

Chuck’s guides and ED manuals/tutorials describe DCS aircraft. The legacy Hornet guide describes its APG-73 radar; public APG-79 material supplies separate AESA context. F-22 references span 1999–2000 development flight tests, 2001 architecture, 2006 rescue equipment, dated operational rules and later manufacturer/USAF accounts. WP00 resolves the intended aircraft configuration before dependent fixes.

| Reference tier | Comparisons | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| F22 documented | 60 | Dated F-22-specific function/behavior; scope and equipment applicability still apply. |
| F16/Hornet analogue | 124 | Named substitute or comparison, not proof of an F-22 error. |
| General flight-physics evidence | 20 | Physical relationships and public capability anchors, not authenticated F-22 curves. |
| General radar/AESA evidence | 13 | Public general radar principles and observable game approximation. |
| General crew-alerting evidence | 6 | Optional general cockpit-design comparator; civil guidance does not establish military aircraft requirements. |

| Closeness label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Matches documented behavior | The narrow stated benchmark agrees. Unknown values or other parts of the system remain outside that match. |
| Partly matches | A stated portion agrees and a concrete remaining difference is identified. |
| Contradicts documented behavior | The stated implementation conflicts with evidence in its stated tier. Check the tier: a physics conflict is not a recovered F-22 manual limit. |
| Missing documented behavior | The cited function/principle has no corresponding behavior in the inspected owned paths; declared era/equipment and host limits still apply. |
| Diverges from selected analogue | Difference from the named alternative or general substitute. Adoption remains explicit. |
| Not assessable from available evidence | No defensible closeness conclusion for this particular property. This is not a failure grade. |

Confidence describes the stated comparison, not the likelihood that the entire aircraft is accurate. The counts are scope bookkeeping, not a weighted fidelity score.

## How to use this guide for the project

Start with WP00, then work through the dependency order below. Open the relevant finding, retain its evidence boundary, and implement the proposed observable behavior. Every case includes normal operation, limits and failure/recovery acceptance. Positive matches are retention criteria; unknowns are evidence/calibration tasks; optional analogue differences require a recorded design choice.

Use a finding ID in each implementation change. Record the chosen baseline/substitute, new source revision, affected dependencies and acceptance evidence. Close only the stated behavior. “Implemented,” “tested” and “F-22 documented” are separate facts. This document proposes changes; it does not mark them completed.

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Resolve configuration/evidence/dependency decisions before dependent implementation. |
| P1 | First implementation tranche: documented functional omissions or a concrete user-path/physical inconsistency. |
| P2 | Follow-on depth and coherent normal/limit/degraded behavior. |
| P3 | Optional/interface/analogue policy choice; not automatically a required F-22 fix. |

### WP00 · Freeze the aircraft and evidence baseline

**Dependencies:** None; baseline decision first.

Choose a dated F-22 configuration and equipment list. Record each supported real behavior, adopted analogue and unresolved parameter before writing fixes. Preserve explicit alternatives when sources conflict.

**Completion evidence:** A configuration sheet identifies era/software/equipment, land-based recovery, optional equipment exclusions and adopted substitutes. No modern requirement is silently treated as fleet-wide fielding.

**Scope:** [AV31](#auth-av31), [AN26](#auth-an26), [AN30](#auth-an30), [AS27](#auth-as27), [AX01](#auth-ax01), [AX09](#auth-ax09), [AX10](#auth-ax10), [AX13](#auth-ax13), [AX14](#auth-ax14).

### Executed analysis probes

The actual captured warning Lua policy was executed in Lua5.1 with synthetic states. It produced a first caution, no new event after acknowledgement while the combined caution stayed true, and a new event after full clear/reassert. Ground or navigation-invalid inputs returned blank policy output; independent native/discrete indications were not exercised. The probe supports those state-path observations only. Comparator-specific voice inhibits and production F-22 behavior remain unresolved. Full inputs/scope/results are retained in the verification companion.

This pass adds **8 further comparisons** and **21 targeted reviews**, anchored to 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT. It tests premises as well as implementation paths. A corrected premise can remove an unnecessary fix; a reproduced code discrepancy can strengthen a narrowly scoped finding without establishing real-aircraft behavior.

### Control-path reproduction scope

Actual captured Lua owners were executed with synthetic parameters and native stubs. The heading probe supplied the checked degree-valued publication contract: 0° acknowledged, while1°,90°,123° and359° applied by that simulated publisher falsely timed out. A dropped NAV receiver left achieved latitude unchanged while a same-ID edit reported ENTERED. The same recognized focused radar format moved its horizontal cursor at primary focus2 and stayed still at3/4/5 in both A/A and A/G, with a healthy synthetic A/G backend. These reproduce the specified state paths; they do not establish native DCS integration, renderer behavior or flight response. Other probes retain their individual scope/results in the verification ledger.

## Uncertainty and calibration register

These are explicit project decisions or evidence gaps. Do not fill them by copying arbitrary comparator numbers and then present the result as documented F-22 behavior. A source-limited estimate can be coherent and useful while remaining an estimate.

| Property | What is known / unresolved | Next decision or evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Aircraft configuration | Historical architecture and emergency equipment are documented; current software/equipment fit is not established by every source. | WP00 selects era/equipment and optional functions; preserve dated applicability. |
| Approach AoA/E-bracket | The mod uses12 degrees; the continuation found a historical F-22 EMD12-degree on-speed anchor and11.5-degree single-engine test-law change. Production applicability and exact bracket/indexer widths remain unknown. | Reconcile the selected-era reference with lift, weight, trim, configuration and cue geometry; do not treat another aircraft’s AoA as the F-22 calibration. [AN04](#auth-an04), [PF16](#auth-pf16), [VG05](#auth-vg05) |
| Thrust, drag, fuel and high-alpha envelope | Public broad capability anchors exist; installed full-condition performance and production curves are unknown. | Use matched-condition sweeps and physically consistent bounded estimates; do not claim validated turn/climb/departure limits. [PF02](#auth-pf02), [PF13](#auth-pf13), [PF19](#auth-pf19) |
| CG and ground effect | Physical dependencies can be checked without secret aircraft curves. | Fix/establish structure first, then estimate magnitude independently. [PF07](#auth-pf07), [PF17](#auth-pf17) |
| AESA timing/detection/scan loss | Electronic agility, resource competition and graceful degradation are public; APG-77 exact scheduling/sensitivity are not. | Use declared observable game tradeoffs; no operational waveform, ECCM or LPI algorithm inference. [AE01](#auth-ae01)–[AE17](#auth-ae17) |
| Radar/network track age | Current configured range/TTL values describe the model, not real detection or memory limits. | Separate observed/received/estimated time and choose explicit display/coast policies. [AS04](#auth-as04), [AS25](#auth-as25) |
| SES, APU and hydraulic capacities | Four main pumps and the APU pump have public ratings; SES reserve, activation criteria, consumer pressure/flow and distribution remain unresolved. | Use bounded source topology and estimates; do not transplant inconsistent rescue-table quantities. [AV15](#auth-av15), [AV26](#auth-av26) |
| Electrical endurance and conversion | 28 V battery domain and 270 V ground interface are compatible; capacity, load and discharge law remain estimated. | Consumer matrix and source-loss behavior first; calibration second. [AV31](#auth-av31), [AX03](#auth-ax03) |
| Oxygen, thermal and warning thresholds | Supply/backup principles are documented; all exact F-22 schedules and colors are not. | Declare thresholds/hysteresis and require valid physical sources; avoid copied engine limits. [AV10](#auth-av10), [AV11](#auth-av11), [P15](#support-p15) |
| CM programs and automation | Programmable manual/semi/automatic roles are historical F-22 evidence; fields, recipes and operational selection are not disclosed. | Choose a generic flat scheme or explicit nested alternative; specify only game edit/sequence/inventory semantics. [AS22](#auth-as22), [CP02](#auth-cp02) |
| Autoland and automatic collision recovery | Carrier ACLS procedures are not a land-based F-22 specification. ### AV01 · Integrated pitch-only thrust vectoring and physical travel

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Matches documented behavior** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** Pratt &amp; Whitney documents this capability directly.

**Reference behavior:** F119 nozzles vector up/down as much as 20 degrees; nozzle management is integrated with F-22 flight controls and regulated by FADEC. [F-22 / F119 · Exceptional Combat Performance / Delivers Unparalleled Aircraft Maneuverability](<https://www.rtx.com/prattwhitney/products/military-engines/f119>).

**Our captured behavior:** A common pitch-derived command drives left/right achieved nozzle states, bounded to ±20 degrees; each nozzle produces a rotated thrust vector. Mach/WOW scheduling reduces available travel.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The narrow documented pitch-axis, maximum-travel and integrated-command behavior matches. The proprietary Mach/gear schedule and reversion behavior remain unknown; they do not lower this narrow match.

**Implementation target:** Retain integrated pitch vectoring with an absolute ±20-degree mechanical bound. Label the mod’s Mach, gear and hydraulic schedules as estimates rather than asserting that the brochure authenticates them.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Production engine capability; no claim that ±20 degrees is available at every flight condition.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** At a supported low-Mach condition, compare command, achieved left/right angle and force direction.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Sweep each mechanical bound and the estimated Mach/gear schedules.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Remove one hydraulic supply; retain independent achieved nozzle states and opposite-engine behavior.

**Dependencies:** TVC command, Per-side hydraulic state, Physical forces and animation.

**Re-audit:** Confirmed. Narrow manufacturer pitch-axis/travel/integration claim remains supported; proprietary schedules are explicitly outside the match.

**Captured implementation:** [EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:36](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:36>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:703](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:703>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1018](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1018>).

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Document pump-to-circuit abstraction and steady pressure/flow at one and two engines.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Exercise concurrent demand against reduced source capacity without assuming the sum of rated flows is always available.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Compare individual pump loss with full circuit loss and recovery.

**Dependencies:** Circuit map, Pump availability, Demand representation, Pressure measurement definition.

**Re-audit:** Qualified. Confirmed four pump specification, but two pressure states can abstract four pumps. Outlet compensation is distinguished from cockpit/consumer pressure.

### PF01 · Dry/augmented thrust and installed-force anchors

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Matches documented behavior** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** F119 manufacturer publishes 35,000-lb thrust class, augmentation and pitch vectoring; no dry/installed engine deck is supplied.

**Reference behavior:** The F119 is an augmented turbofan in the 35,000-pound thrust class. That class is not an exact net installed thrust at every altitude/Mach. [F-22 / F119 · Exceptional Combat Performance / Delivers Unparalleled Aircraft Maneuverability](<https://www.rtx.com/prattwhitney/products/military-engines/f119>).

**Our captured behavior:** Static anchors are 112,654 N dry and 155,688 N augmented per engine; the latter is approximately 35,000 lbf. A smooth airspeed blend replaces static anchors with Mach tables, then density and damage scale force.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The nominal augmented anchor matches the published class. The dry anchor, ram/installation schedule and full force envelope remain estimates; they are not validated by this numerical coincidence.

**Implementation target:** Retain a traceable 35,000-lb-class augmented anchor while identifying dry thrust and each installed correction separately. Calibrate available matched-condition evidence without treating class thrust as a constant flight thrust.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Narrow class-anchor match; exact dry/installed thrust unknown.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Read achieved dry and augmented force at a declared static standard condition.; Compare the two independent engines at equal throttle/state.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Sweep the static-to-forward-speed blend through 100 m/s.; Separate pressure altitude, temperature and Mach in reported conditions.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Cut one engine and verify only its force disappears.; Restore health without silently restoring throttle state.

### AN01 · Independent HUD/SFG navigation-source choice

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Missing documented behavior** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

[Real F-22A · p 36 §7.9.1.1](<https://static.e-publishing.af.mil/production/1/af_a3/publication/afman11-2f-22av3/afman11-2f-22av3.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Navigation_System constructs one INS_Model estimate. HUD attitude and ADI attitude are fed from common base-data pitch/roll, with no captured GINS1/GINS2/SFG selection or independent-reference state.

**Closeness and exact difference:** A second attitude drawing would not reproduce the documented choice of independent navigation reference.

**Implementation target:** Represent two independently valid attitude/navigation reference channels and selectable HUD/SFG sources. Implement the documented independence; do not invent unpublished sensor-error numbers.

**Adoption decision:** direct baseline. Independent GINS references are explicitly described in the dated F-22 procedure.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Real F-22 documented degraded-flight behavior; direct baseline requirement, with 2018 edition caveat.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** HUD uses reference 1; SFG uses independently selected reference 2.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Selecting the same source on both views does not imply independence.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Fail reference 1; independently valid reference 2 remains usable and labelled.

**Dependencies:** Navigation-source ownership, Standby flight-group presentation.

### AN02 · Positive-position updates and navigation-quality indication

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Partly matches** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** AFMAN11-2F-22AV3 (2018) section 4.1.3 defines an INS update as establishing positive position by visual reference, TACAN, GPS or onboard radar; NAV STATUS GPS HIGH suffices. It does not describe an observation/accept interface or require a manual correction to the inertial filter.

**Reference behavior:** The pilot can establish positive position and recognize a high-quality GPS navigation state. The dated enroute rule permits no more than 1.5hours between such updates. Viper FIX independently documents a freeze/inspect/accept correction workflow, but that is a separate optional analogue, not an F-22 requirement established by this paragraph. [Real F-22A · p 26 §4.1.3](<https://static.e-publishing.af.mil/production/1/af_a3/publication/afman11-2f-22av3/afman11-2f-22av3.pdf>), [DCS F-16C benchmark · pp 760–761 FIX/overfly update](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Aided INS_Model uses simulator position, and the native TACAN/route views provide position-crosscheck information. Flight_Guidance exposes GPS aiding/alignment status, but the captured path has no receiver-derived GPS HIGH quality state. There is no manual observation/accept interface into INS_Model; its absence alone is not a contradiction of the F-22 operational paragraph.

**Closeness and exact difference:** GPS-aided position and TACAN information support positive-position awareness. A pilot toggle and an AID status are not independently established GPS HIGH quality, and the operating rule does not authenticate a mandatory manual INS-update page.

**Implementation target:** Make navigation quality, aiding availability and last positive-position check explicit. Preserve visual/TACAN/GPS/radar crosschecks; only add a manual fix correction interface if adopting the Viper workflow as a declared simulation extension.

**Adoption decision:** direct baseline with optional extension. Positive-position/quality behavior is direct; a Viper FIX transaction is optional.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Direct F-22 dated positive-position/quality behavior; the optional Viper FIX interface is not a proven F-22 cockpit requirement.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Aided good-quality navigation is recognized; TACAN/visual checks can establish position.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** GPS aiding commanded on with unavailable receiver does not assert GPS HIGH.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Aiding loss/reacquisition changes quality and retains clearly identified inertial navigation.

**Dependencies:** Receiver-quality model, Navigation state.

**Re-audit:** Corrected. Full section 4.1.3 defines positive-position checks; the prior row overclaimed that it proves a mandatory manual INS correction workflow.

Independent nested Viper timing is an optional alternate model, not proof that the Hornet-like structure is inaccurate.

Preserve three banks as an explicit mod estimate. Offer independent per-type BQ/BI/SQ/SI only as an optional deeper model, without real tactical presets.

### CP01 · Independent chaff/flare quantities and intra-burst timing

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Diverges from selected analogue** · Confidence: high · Priority: P3 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The reviewed F-22 architecture account does not disclose these program fields, limits or cockpit control rules.

**Reference behavior:** Viper CHAFF and FLARE pages independently expose BQ (items within a burst), BI (spacing within that burst), SQ (burst count) and SI (spacing between bursts). [DCS F-16C benchmark · pp 591–592 field definitions and separate category pages](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Each mod program has independent chaff and flare counts, but both types are released in the same scheduler event with no independent intra-burst item timing. There is one shared interval.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Independent counts already exist; independent per-type timing and per-item burst spacing do not. A batched quantity request is not a BI-controlled sequence.

**Implementation target:** If adopting the Viper-style model, store separate per-type burst quantity/interval and repeat-group quantity/interval. Use neutral user-defined game presets, not published operational/default patterns.

**Adoption decision:** optional alternative. Independent nested Viper timing is a deeper alternative, not required in the chosen flat model.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic DCS game-program semantics only. No threat-specific recipes, operational defaults, effectiveness values or defensive selection algorithms are proposed.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Independent chaff/flare fields generate distinct per-item/per-group event timelines.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Zero category quantity and zero/invalid interval bounds are defined without unbounded loops.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Interrupted sequence follows declared no-surprise-resume contract.

**Dependencies:** Optional schema decision, Sequence scheduler.

### CP02 · Flat Hornet program versus nested Viper burst/salvo structure

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Partly matches** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The reviewed F-22 architecture account does not disclose these program fields, limits or cockpit control rules.

**Reference behavior:** Hornet manual editing uses CHAF, FLAR, RPT and INT with SAVE. This is a flatter schema than the Viper BQ/BI/SQ/SI hierarchy; the cited Hornet passages do not fully settle whether RPT means total cycles or additional repeats. [DCS F/A-18C benchmark · p 611 full program-edit steps](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C benchmark · p 410 ARM/programming paragraph](<https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/upload/iblock/8d7/2s3e89jqknz7xmti8hrhe1bjt2uw1s3e/DCS%20FA-18C%20Early%20Access%20Guide%20EN.pdf>), [DCS F-16C benchmark · p 591 BQ/BI/SQ/SI definitions](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** The four fields chaff/flare/interval/repetitions closely resemble Hornet program fields. repetitions is explicitly total scheduler events: bursts starts at repetitions and decrements once per event that releases anything. Each category count cycles 0-4, shared interval selects 0.1/0.25/0.5/1/2seconds, and total events cycles 1-8. Both categories zero is rejected when the scheduler reads the bank. These are field capacities, not recommended programs.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The existing schema is substantially Hornet-like, not an empty/unrelated program model. It does not implement the separate Viper timing hierarchy; the documents do not justify silently equating repeats with total events.

**Implementation target:** Select a declared game schema. Retain the simple Hornet-like model or add the deeper independent timing model; label total cycles versus additional repeats explicitly and define whether the first event is included. Avoid treating Viper field count as a universal F-22 requirement.

**Adoption decision:** selected analogue. Flat Hornet-like fields are the chosen generic game program model, with explicit total-event semantics.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic DCS game-program semantics only. No threat-specific recipes, operational defaults, effectiveness values or defensive selection algorithms are proposed.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** A neutral user-created test program produces exactly its displayed total cycles.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** One total cycle means one event; zero-category and empty program behavior is explicit.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Partial exhaustion does not change what the UI means by configured total cycles.

**Dependencies:** [AS21](#auth-as21), Sequence display.

**Re-audit:** New case. Complete cited passages and the fresh pinned source retain this narrow behavioral comparison; analogy and public-evidence limits remain explicit.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Changing the visible PROG selection changes which bank is edited, but not what the normal up action runs. Bank count itself has no verified F-22 specification.

Do not call the Viper direct-access bank 6 the same thing as physical BYP mode: the guide uses ambiguous labels there.

**Adoption decision:** selected analogue. Normal selected-program execution and separately labelled direct access are chosen common comparator behavior.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic DCS game-program semantics only. No threat-specific recipes, operational defaults, effectiveness values or defensive selection algorithms are proposed.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Change PROG/STEP then normal dispense; executed bank agrees with selection.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Direct-access button intentionally uses its bank without changing normal selection unless declared.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Rejected/unavailable program is visible and does not fall back silently.

### CP06 · Consent grant/revoke controls future automatic execution

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Diverges from selected analogue** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The reviewed F-22 architecture account does not disclose these program fields, limits or cockpit control rules.

**Reference behavior:** Viper SEMI/AUTO requires CMS-aft authorization and CMS-right revokes it. ED Hornet S/A waits for pilot initiation of a recommended program; AUTO initially defaults to consent, continues its automatic program while the source condition persists, and lets the pilot revoke/re-enable consent. Manual selected-program access remains a separate path. These are different initial-consent conventions, not interchangeable labels, and do not imply that consent-revoke cancels a manual sequence. **Our captured behavior:** CMS-down/right only store F22_CM_CONSENT=1/0; the scheduler never reads it. They do not authorize, prevent or stop any release, and bindings honestly label them Reserved.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The visible pilot action has no dispenser effect. This is not evidence that the manual sequence should be canceled by consent-off; that would be a separate policy.

**Implementation target:** Choose the Hornet initial-consent/revoke convention for the declared generic game AUTO model and a distinct consent-triggered SEMI start. Make the chosen authorization state visible and gate only SEMI/AUTO release; manual release is independent. Define active-sequence cancellation separately rather than inferring it from consent-off. No real threat-selection algorithm is prescribed.

**Adoption decision:** selected analogue. Hornet consent/revoke provides the provisional interaction model, without importing threat-selection algorithms.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic DCS game-program semantics only. No threat-specific recipes, operational defaults, effectiveness values or defensive selection algorithms are proposed.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** SEMI consent starts only the displayed recommendation; entering AUTO visibly starts with the chosen Hornet consent-enabled state.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Revoke prevents further automatic starts; current-sequence behavior and manual-release independence are separately declared.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Power/mode reset displays the actual reset authorization state rather than silently retaining stale consent.

**Dependencies:** [CP05](#auth-cp05), Consent state owner.

### VG01 · Fuel/store redistribution changes angular inertia as well as mass and CG

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Not assessable from available evidence** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** F-22 fuel capacity/external tanks are public; exact tank geometry and production inertia tensors are not.

**Reference behavior:** Rotational inertia depends on mass distribution and squared distance from each axis. Equal total mass and CG need not imply equal response to the same torque. [General flight/utility physics · 17](<https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sp-4540.pdf>), [F-22 · Internal/external fuel capacity](<https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104506/f-22-raptor/About-Us/f-22-raptor/>).

**Our captured behavior:** Burn/refill transactions carry position and mass, but every queued moment-of-inertia change is zero. Current inertia is received from the host. The included API says DCS performs internal mass/CG/inertia calculations, so zero local MOI does not prove the host keeps inertia fixed.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The open issue is the complete host-plus-EFM angular response after redistribution, distinct from the already identified moving wing force point. The host may infer point-mass inertia from the supplied location; that contract must be established before adding another correction.

**Implementation target:** Establish which inertia contributions DCS derives from position/mass and which the EFM must supply, then preserve mass, first moment and angular inertia consistently. Use estimated lumped tank/store geometry; do not invent a measured F-22 tensor.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic rigid-body relation; host contract and production numbers unresolved.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare equal-mass/equal-CG cases with different spanwise fuel/store distribution and the same small applied moment.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Compare partial/full tanks and a mirrored asymmetric installation without assuming current inertia has changed merely because mass changed.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Remove/refill a station and verify host and EFM each account for the change exactly once.

**Dependencies:** DCS mass/inertia contract, Tank/store geometry abstraction, Host current inertia.

**Re-audit:** New case. Prior UV15/PF07 covered mass transactions and force moment arms; this isolates rotational inertia and angular acceleration.

**Captured implementation:** [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:179](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:179>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1324](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1324>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1074](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1074>), [EFM/include/FM/wHumanCustomPhysicsAPI.h:271](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/include/FM/wHumanCustomPhysicsAPI.h:271>).

### VG02 · Air-relative force is invariant to a uniform ground/wind translation

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Matches documented behavior** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** No F-22-specific coefficient is required for the reference-frame relationship.

**Reference behavior:** At fixed achieved configuration in free air, aerodynamic force depends on aircraft velocity relative to air. Adding the same uniform velocity to aircraft and air leaves that aerodynamic condition unchanged. Tire/ground behavior instead depends on motion relative to the runway. [General flight/utility physics · Ground reference / wind speed / airspeed / wind tunnel equivalence](<https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/relative-velocity/>), [General flight/utility physics · Nomenclature: true and ground speed](<https://society-of-flight-test-engineers.github.io/quarto-handbook/04-pitot-statics.html>).

**Our captured behavior:** World velocity minus world wind supplies aerodynamic speed/Mach/q. The body-state callback independently subtracts body wind for drag direction. Horizontal world velocity supplies ground-speed steering/brake gates. These are the correct narrow frame distinctions; consistency of the two host callback vectors has not been flown.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Both relevant relative velocities are represented instead of treating groundspeed as aerodynamic speed. A host callback orientation/sign mismatch is still possible and is not ruled out by reading the subtraction alone.

**Implementation target:** Retain the frame distinction. Verify airborne aerodynamic-force invariance at fixed achieved configuration with ground-interaction gates inactive and matching body/world vectors. Separately preserve wind-dependent takeoff/landing groundspeed, automatic ground schedules and wheel motion.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Narrow airborne mathematical/frame match at fixed achieved configuration; no numerical F-22 force validation or invariance requirement for changed ground interactions.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Airborne, hold achieved configuration, air-relative velocity/AoA/density and all other force inputs fixed, with ground-interaction gates inactive. Translate world aircraft and wind velocity equally and provide matching body vectors; aerodynamic outputs should agree.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** In the isolated airborne case, compare crosswind/tailwind and near-zero airspeed/groundspeed without changing achieved configuration.; Evaluate ground roll separately: with the runway fixed, changed groundspeed may legitimately alter automatic flap targets, braking, steering and wheel forces. Do not require those outputs to be invariant.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Provide inconsistent or invalid body/world inputs as diagnostic cases, not as claims that real wind changes aircraft coefficients.

**Dependencies:** Host body/world coordinate contract, Wind callbacks, Ground contact.

**Re-audit:** New case. PF20 addressed atmospheric sensitivity; this isolates wind invariance and ground-relative versus air-relative consumers.

**Captured implementation:** [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:372](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:372>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:226](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:226>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:470](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:470>), [EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:366](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:366>).

### VG03 · Signed normal load and gravity compensation remain coherent in bank/inverted flight

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Not assessable from available evidence** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** F-22 exact acceleration-sensor processing is unknown. The selected DCS Viper FLCS explicitly uses normal acceleration as a control input.

**Reference behavior:** An accelerometer measures local specific force including gravity reaction; indicated normal load is not generally obtained from a body-axis inertial acceleration by adding the same upright constant in every attitude. [General flight/utility physics · Definition: local specific force and gravity reaction](<https://support.sbg-systems.com/sc/kb/latest/inertial-measurements-units/accelerometers>), [DCS F-16CM Block 50 / F110 · 665](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** EFM g is assigned ay/9.81 + 1 and drives load reduction and related states. HUD peak g instead reads the base sensor. The API labels ay body-coordinate linear acceleration but does not state gravity treatment; no measured upright/inverted/free-fall comparison establishes the actual output error.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The fixed +1 convention needs host-semantic validation, particularly because the limiter and pilot indication use different producers. It is not justified to declare a universal two-g error from the SDK comment alone.

**Implementation target:** Determine whether the callback supplies inertial acceleration or specific force, then use an attitude-consistent normal-load quantity for the owned limiter. Reconcile the displayed producer at the same physical condition; keep F-22 sensor/filter details estimated.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Host acceleration semantics unresolved; generic specific-force relationship only.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare stationary/upright and ordinary level-flight normal load against host indication.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Compare steady inverted flight, steep bank and a ballistic low-load segment while tracking the exact callback meaning.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Inject invalid sensor data separately from real load and verify it does not become a valid limiter demand.

**Dependencies:** DCS acceleration convention, Body attitude, Owned g and HUD data producers.

**Re-audit:** New case. PF11 compared peak and sustainable g; this examines the actual sensed input and signed gravity compensation feeding that limiter.

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Partly matches** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** Rainey/Kohn describe this directly for the 1998 EMD configuration; exact current production schedule remains unknown.

**Reference behavior:** The historical F-22 uses ordinary control surfaces for braking: cruise combines ailerons up, flaperons down and rudders out; power approach/air refueling use the rudders only. [F-22 EMD 4001/4002 · Flights with speed brakes; paragraphs 25–26](<https://man.fas.org/dod-101/sys/ac/docs/f-22-emd-paper.htm>).

**Our captured behavior:** A generic airbrake scalar adds drag; both rudder arguments receive the same directional rudder command and ailerons receive opposing roll angles. Separate airbrake arguments are written, but the EFM has no cruise/PA/AR mixed-surface force allocation. EDM argument semantics can still add visual effects and were not inspected.

**Closeness and exact difference:** A braking request produces drag, but the documented historical configuration-dependent achieved-surface relationship is not represented in the owned force model. This is not proof that every visible door/surface animation is wrong.

**Implementation target:** For an explicitly applicable profile, represent the documented surface groups and retain consistent achieved mixing, forces and drawing. Establish EDM semantics first; keep current production angles, priorities and transient compensation as declared estimates.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Historical EMD capability, not a command to recreate its test-era defects or claim production calibration.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare brake request in cruise, power approach and refueling configuration with commanded/achieved individual surfaces.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Combine braking with pitch/roll/yaw and saturating commands, preserving an explicit estimated priority.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Lose one effector or hydraulic source and keep braking/trim changes tied to achieved surfaces.

**Dependencies:** Configuration state, EDM argument mapping, Surface mixing, Force allocation.

**Re-audit:** New case. UV27 noted generic speed-brake uncertainty; this adds exact primary-source CR/PA/AR distinctions and the owned force-versus-animation boundary.

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Contradicts documented behavior** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**Reference behavior:** Aerodynamic force depends on the surviving effective surface and its achieved configuration. A declared destroyed control element cannot continue supplying its full unaffected owned control force merely because its drawing is damaged. [General aircraft flight physics · L=CL*rho*V²*A/2](<https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/lift-equation/>), [F-22 EMD test aircraft · 1](<https://sfte-ec.org/sfteecold/data/Abstract/A2000-II-02.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 / F404 · 652](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Damage cells 25/26 and 51/52 are registered. The callback stores them but only aggregates wing/tail/engine subsets. Aileron forces have no corresponding integrity factor; separate elevon integrity fields are reset to 1 but never changed by damage. Thus those direct cell changes leave their owned force terms unchanged; native secondary damage events remain a separate host question.

**Closeness and exact difference:** For the specifically registered control cells, the owned physical force ignores the recorded loss. This does not claim an authentic F-22 fracture percentage or that the host can never cause additional coupled damage.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Narrow owned force response to the mod’s existing damage contract, not a real structural-survival deck.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Reduce one named aileron or elevator cell and inspect its force/moment at otherwise equal command/state.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Mirror left/right cases, partial loss, jam versus lost surface and combined hydraulic loss.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Repair restores the supported effectiveness once without healing an unrelated retained fault.

**Dependencies:** Damage-cell contract, Achieved control surfaces, Owned force terms, Repair.

### VG07 · Accumulator fluid use differs from wheel-braking heat

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Partly matches** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** Historical F-22 rescue diagrams identify wheel-well accumulators but do not disclose the exact brake reserve deck.

**Reference behavior:** Hydraulic storage releases pressurized fluid as system demand draws volume and also compensates leakage. The wheel-brake heat generated while rolling is a different energy account. [General flight/utility physics · 3](<https://www.parker.com/content/dam/Parker-com/Literature/Accumulator---Cooler-Division---Americas/Catalogs---Bulletins/Making_the_Choice_Accumulators_1660-USA.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C · 59](<https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/upload/iblock/8d7/2s3e89jqknz7xmti8hrhe1bjt2uw1s3e/DCS%20FA-18C%20Early%20Access%20Guide%20EN.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** The normalized reserve is depleted by elapsed time and pedal demand multiplied by ground speed; applying/releasing brakes repeatedly while stationary adds no pedal-dependent depletion. Holding pressure while rolling consumes reserve continuously even without another stroke. This is a reserve proxy, not a fluid-displacement model.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Finite reserve/recharge exists, but application-volume and thermal work are conflated in the speed-dependent depletion term. Leakage can legitimately deplete a stationary reserve, so the small continuous leak is not itself an error.

**Implementation target:** Use a declared fluid-demand/pressure reserve abstraction for application/release and leakage, separately from brake heat. Keep F-22 accumulator quantity, usable applications and valve behavior estimated; do not copy Hornet pressure markings.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Generic hydraulic conservation and selected DCS workflow; exact F-22 reserve unknown.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare repeated applications with a held application at rest and the same declared leakage.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Compare low/high-speed rolling hold without inventing a real available-application count.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Lose main pressure, consume reserve, restore a source and recharge according to one pressure/fluid model.

**Dependencies:** Brake demand transitions, Accumulator state, Leakage, Separate thermal state.

**Re-audit:** New case. UV19/AV34 distinguish reserve and heat generally; this isolates what consumes stored pressure during repeated stationary applications versus rolling hold.

**Captured implementation:** [EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:106](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:106>), [EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:107](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:107>), [EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:114](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:114>).

### VG08 · HUD CAS and internal EAS schedules are explicitly different quantities

**Basis:** General flight-physics evidence · **Partly matches** · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** Production F-22 configuration threshold quantities are not established by the public references.

**Reference behavior:** EAS is TAS scaled by density ratio; CAS is derived from compressible pitot impact pressure at standard sea-level reference. They agree in a limited low-speed regime and diverge at higher Mach/altitude. [General flight/utility physics · Sections 4.1–4.4](<https://society-of-flight-test-engineers.github.io/quarto-handbook/04-pitot-statics.html>), [DCS F/A-18C · 58](<https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/upload/iblock/8d7/2s3e89jqknz7xmti8hrhe1bjt2uw1s3e/DCS%20FA-18C%20Early%20Access%20Guide%20EN.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** HUD and AFCS use compressible CAS. Gear commands, high-lift and trim schedules use TAS*sqrt(rho/1.225) while variables call it IAS. In a static arithmetic example at 30,000 Pa/250 K, 275 kt EAS corresponds to about 288.6 kt CAS; this is not a DCS flight result.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Both formulas can be useful for different purposes; the problem is an unspecified displayed-versus-scheduled speed convention. It is not valid to replace every aerodynamic q-based gain with CAS blindly.

**Implementation target:** Assign each limit, configuration schedule and pilot display an explicit speed quantity. Where a pilot-facing KIAS/KCAS rule is intended, use a consistent converted value; retain EAS/q for rules actually defined by dynamic pressure and label estimated thresholds.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Internal quantity distinction is demonstrated algebraically; actual F-22 thresholds remain unknown.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare HUD/AFCS CAS with gear/high-lift/trim schedule inputs at a declared atmosphere.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Repeat at sea-level low Mach and higher altitude/Mach; preserve intended q-based gains.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** A pressure or air-data fault must not silently turn one quantity into another valid indication.

**Dependencies:** CAS/EAS definitions, Atmosphere, Pilot-facing limits, Configuration schedules.

**Re-audit:** New case. PF20 noted the approximation broadly; this traces the simultaneous CAS/EAS owners and a concrete internal threshold/display difference.

### VG12 · Collective and differential surface demands compete at saturation

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Matches documented behavior** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** F-22 integrated controls and physical nozzle bounds are public; production allocation priorities across simultaneous commands are not disclosed.

**Our captured behavior:** Left/right elevon commands are clamp(pitch minus roll) and clamp(pitch plus roll). With both normalized demands at 1, the pair becomes 0 and 1: average pitch contribution falls from 1 to 0.5 while roll contribution remains 0.5. Separate aileron and TVC paths still contribute; this arithmetic is not a flight response result.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Collective/differential mixing and finite travel exist. The actual tradeoff is source-visible but its correctness cannot be authenticated from an undisclosed F-22 allocation law; simultaneous-axis performance remains distinct from single-axis limits.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare pure pitch, pure roll and combined commands using achieved surfaces and total moments.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Sweep all demand corners, reversals and saturation without assuming single-axis maxima add.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Repeat with one effector/source lost and retain an explicit estimated residual priority.

**Dependencies:** Achieved surfaces, TVC, Combined moment accounting, Declared allocation policy.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** A deliberate permanent-disconnect control remains distinct; combined vertical modes follow a separately declared policy.

### SG01 · Radar cue, seeker acquisition and autonomous IR tracking are distinct

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Partly matches** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The published fit includes infrared missiles and integrated stores control; exact F-22 cage/slave/uncage transitions are not published in these references.

**Reference behavior:** Viper separates BORE/SLAVE cueing from seeker acquisition; Hornet no-radar employment requires a seeker search/lock indication. A radar line of sight is not itself an IR lock. [F-22 design as published 2001 · PDF p 10, section 32.3.5](<https://www.helitavia.com/avionics/TheAvionicsHandbook_Cap_32.pdf>), [F-22 · Armament](<https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104506/f-22-raptor/About-Us/f-22-raptor/>), [DCS F-16CM Block 50 · pp 538-540](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · pp 580-581](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** The native IR adapter supplies radar slaving only while the uncaged seeker is not already tracking. A real native tracking result drives F22_IR_LOCK; an acquired seeker is left autonomous rather than reset to each new radar cue. Uncage request is retained before detection, with a custom strength threshold controlling head release.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The separation is a genuine positive. This does not establish exact F-22 head-release thresholds, automatic cage behavior or modern missile cueing fit. An acquired IR object need not be the newly selected radar object.

**Implementation target:** Preserve independent radar-cue and seeker-track states. Show actual seeker acquisition and its LOS; a subsequent radar retarget should not silently assert that the already autonomous IR seeker tracks that new contact. Declare the chosen recage/re-slave procedure as a simulation estimate.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** The named DCS model is an explicit comparison or optional substitute. F-22 control details are unknown unless the specific published fact is stated; no operational algorithms or recipes are inferred.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Cue an exposed selected seeker, obtain an actual IR track, then change radar selection: radar and IR indications continue to show their respective sources.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Radar cue without IR detection does not show IR TRACK; radar-off leaves valid autonomous seeker state independent.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Recage, store change or seeker loss clears/restarts the intended state without carrying the previous object as a fresh acquisition.

**Dependencies:** AS28-AS29, Selected missile installation, Seeker observation validity.

**Re-audit:** New case. New interaction comparison beyond the prior feature-level scope; complete cited paths inspected in the 04:17:52 capture.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Hold release while changing station/type: the next store does not launch solely because selection changed.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Loss/restoration of seeker power or station availability cannot replay the old press; the pilot receives a clear current-state cue.

### SG03 · Failed moving-target acquisition can become an undisclosed fixed terrain track

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Not assessable from available evidence** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** Published F-22 SAR/surface-designation capability does not establish a GMTT acquisition-failure or fixed-point fallback procedure.

**Reference behavior:** Hornet GMTT is presented as tracking the selected moving target with speed/heading/vector information. Viper describes a tracked target becoming SPI and explicit LOS-loss memory. Neither passage establishes that unsuccessful object acquisition should silently be presented as a moving-object track. [F-22A modernization increments · Printed p 185, Increment 3.1 context](<https://www.dote.osd.mil/Portals/97/pub/reports/FY2018/other/2018DOTEAnnualReport.pdf?ver=2019-08-21-155621-540>), [F-22 design as published 2001 · PDF p 8, section 32.3.2](<https://www.helitavia.com/avionics/TheAvionicsHandbook_Cap_32.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · pp 253-254](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F-16CM Block 50 · p 237](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** After 3 s unsuccessful native acquisition, terrain-visible fallback sets fixed=true with selected.id=0 and selected_type=3. The native publisher marks a fixed point valid. AG_Radar_System ignores that type when selecting display mode: GMT becomes GMTT (SEA becomes SEAT), but F22_AG_FIXED_TRACK is asserted only in MAP mode. A terrain point can therefore appear as a track with zero speed rather than a disclosed fallback.

**Closeness and exact difference:** A successful fixed-coordinate fallback is not a successful moving-object acquisition. The code knows the distinction but the mode/fixed-track publication can discard it. The cited successful-track procedures do not settle the exact Hornet or F-22 failed-acquisition fallback labeling, so the proposed distinction is a transparent game presentation choice rather than a demonstrated real-aircraft contradiction.

**Implementation target:** Carry the native fixed-versus-object type into the mission/display state. Label a terrain hold as such or return to search under the adopted procedure; do not show a confirmed moving-object track merely because a fallback coordinate exists.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** The named DCS model is an explicit comparison or optional substitute. F-22 control details are unknown unless the specific published fact is stated; no operational algorithms or recipes are inferred.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Successful vehicle acquisition displays its observed object motion and identity.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Acquire empty terrain from GMT/SEA: a valid fallback remains an explicitly fixed coordinate, with no invented target speed/vector.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** An obscured or failed fallback returns to a clear search/acquisition-failed state; a later real object requires new observation/association.

**Dependencies:** [AS18](#auth-as18), Coordinate versus object provenance, Selected ground-radar analogue.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Release a deliberately captured station assignment while a separate live sensor designation updates: the assigned mission remains identifiable.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** For a live TOO-like assignment, a meaningful target change follows the declared cancel/reconsent rule.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Changing station mission, selected store or clearing the assigned target cancels old consent and any pending release.

### SG12 · Internal-bay IR sensing is not automatically equivalent to an exposed external rail

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Not assessable from available evidence** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** USAF identifies internal side-bay IR carriage; AFTC documents a movable AIM-9X launcher/skate development change. Exact production exposure, launch and LOAL controls remain unknown.

**Reference behavior:** The Hornet/Viper seeker procedures assume their selected installation can observe the scene; they do not establish F-22 internal-bay exposure choreography. Applying external-rail sensing unchanged to an enclosed store requires an explicit simulation assumption. [F-22 · Armament, internal side bays](<https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104506/f-22-raptor/About-Us/f-22-raptor/>), [F-22 AIM-9X development test · Official indexed May 17 2012 test event](<https://www.aftc.af.mil/About-Us/History/On-This-Day-in-Test-History/Article-Display-Test-History/Article/2561036/may-17-2012-the-f-22-combined-test-force-completed-the-first-aim-9x-separation/>), [F-22 design as published 2001 · PDF p 10, launcher and bay SMS roles](<https://www.helitavia.com/avionics/TheAvionicsHandbook_Cap_32.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · pp 580-581](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F-16CM Block 50 · p 540](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Native IR enablement uses SRM mode, main power and a loaded selected station. At construction the mount is advanced and clear_observation_aperture moves the observation point outside a fixed airframe box. Neither this eligibility nor aperture placement reads achieved bay/launcher exposure. Weapon_System separately opens bays only under its airborne/armed release-or-uncage policy. A powered SAFE/closed-bay seeker can therefore remain enabled without an owned exposure gate; actual host occlusion and visual launcher mapping have not been measured.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The code decouples optical-observation eligibility from achieved internal-store exposure. Exact F-22 timing and native occlusion remain unassessed, so the presence of a lock must not be declared correct or impossible solely from the closed-door animation. This is a specific integration assumption requiring qualification, not a recovered launcher mechanism.

**Implementation target:** Tie the declared sensing aperture to a qualified achieved-exposure state, or visibly document the compatibility approximation. A stored radar cue may remain available while actual optical acquisition is unavailable. Do not copy Hornet external-rail readiness or invent production F-22 launcher angles, rates or LOAL capability.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** The named DCS model is an explicit comparison or optional substitute. F-22 control details are unknown unless the specific published fact is stated; no operational algorithms or recipes are inferred.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** For the chosen exposed internal-store state, native seeker LOS corresponds to the represented launcher geometry.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Closed/unexposed or jammed configuration does not silently provide an externally positioned optical sensor unless that approximation is explicitly selected.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Exposure loss, station swap and restoration clear/reacquire observations according to the chosen game model without reusing a stale lock.

**Dependencies:** SG01-SG02, [SC29](#support-sc29), EDM/host aperture qualification, Selected missile installation.

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Missing documented behavior** · Confidence: high for captured state path; limited for production F-22 applicability · Priority: P2 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** A primary AFFTC EMD account identifies an airspeed ICAW; it does not publish a production trigger schedule.

**Reference behavior:** The EMD pilot was given an approaching-overspeed airspeed alert. [F-22 EMD · Envelope Expansion Testing, AIRSPEED ICAW paragraph](<https://man.fas.org/dod-101/sys/ac/docs/f-22-emd-paper.htm>), [DCS F/A-18C · p 42 distinction between warning/caution indications and malfunction](<https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/upload/iblock/8d7/2s3e89jqknz7xmti8hrhe1bjt2uw1s3e/DCS%20FA-18C%20Early%20Access%20Guide%20EN.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** The owned warning policy has terrain, altitude, FCS and aggregate caution calls. IAS/Mach appear in flight data, but no owned approaching-overspeed alert state was found in the warning/EFM/HUD paths. Registration speed limits and aerodynamic forces are separate properties.

**Closeness and exact difference:** A speed indication and a configured maximum do not implement the documented attention cue. This is scoped to owned paths; any host warning contribution has not been established.

**Implementation target:** For the selected profile, expose an airspeed-limit state with a declared provisional CAS/Mach/configuration envelope and hysteresis. Keep warning, aerodynamic response and actual damage distinct. Production F-22 trigger values, exact words and lead time remain unresolved.

**Requirement basis:** Dated F-22 function

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Historical EMD function supports the role; current production thresholds and host-native contribution remain unverified.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** In an adopted clean configuration, enter/leave a declared provisional speed-attention region and get one coherent indication.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** CAS and Mach limits are evaluated separately; ground/gear/store configuration changes do not silently use an unrelated clean limit.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Invalid airspeed is indicated as unavailable instead of either a valid overspeed or an all-clear; restore without a false crossing.

**Dependencies:** Air-data validity, Selected aircraft limit baseline, HUD/alert state.

Splitting validity by family is a selected design inference; independent native/discrete annunciators are outside the probe.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Remove HUD/navigation validity while preserving a valid equipment-fault source; only dependent alerts become unavailable.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Restore navigation without erasing, replaying or falsely acknowledging the independent fault.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** An urgent noncancellable warning cannot be dismissed by ordinary caution acknowledgement.

**Basis:** General crew-alerting evidence · **Diverges from selected analogue** · Confidence: high for captured state path; limited for production F-22 applicability · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The exact F-22 occurrence/re-alert policy is undisclosed; repeated fault recognition is judged against the chosen comparator.

**Reference behavior:** Hornet master caution responds to caution indications; general alerting guidance preserves recognition of later occurrences after acknowledgement. [DCS F/A-18C · p 42 master caution onset/reset](<https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/upload/iblock/8d7/2s3e89jqknz7xmti8hrhe1bjt2uw1s3e/DCS%20FA-18C%20Early%20Access%20Guide%20EN.pdf>), [General transport-airplane design guidance · Appendix 2 section 3.g(6) subsequent-fault rearm](<https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_25.1322-1.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** Five causes are ORed into one caution boolean. caution_ack remains true as long as that boolean stays true. A newly added generator/hydraulic/etc. cause does not reset it while another acknowledged cause remains. The captured policy probe yields no new event for that unchanged aggregate, but re-annunciates after the entire aggregate clears and returns.

**Closeness and exact difference:** Fault identity and occurrence are lost before acknowledgement logic. This is more specific than a generic caution feature inventory: the interface cannot distinguish a fresh cause from the previously acknowledged cause.

**Implementation target:** Pass stable cause IDs and occurrence counters into attention arbitration. Acknowledge the occurrences actually presented, retain active acknowledged faults, and re-alert on a newly qualifying cause without demanding that every previous cause first disappear.

**Requirement basis:** Explicit substitute/adoption decision; general civil guidance is not a military-aircraft rule

**Applicability / unresolved details:** The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Fault A produces attention; acknowledge A; adding B produces a new adopted attention event while A remains active.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Repeated samples of unchanged A do not masquerade as new occurrences; A+B resolved/recurred have intentional rules.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Source invalidity, power loss and mission reset do not revive old acknowledgements or erase a genuine new occurrence.

**Basis:** General crew-alerting evidence · **Partly matches** · Confidence: high for captured state path; limited for production F-22 applicability · Priority: P3 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

**Review update — 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT:** Reread Viperp 157 explicitly permits muting all voice messages with VOICE MESSAGE INHIBIT. The mod’s global own-voice mute is therefore a supported aircraft-analogue policy option. The FAA-style persistent suppression/volume recommendations remain optional general context, distinct from whether global mute itself is permitted. [Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/UFC_Controller.lua:147](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/UFC_Controller.lua:147>), [Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/Pilot_Warning_System.lua:157](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/Pilot_Warning_System.lua:157>).

**F-22 evidence boundary:** The F-22 mute availability, minimum volume and indication policy are not established by the reviewed sources.

**Reference behavior:** Viper VOICE MESSAGE INHIBIT mutes all voice messages. General FAA suppression-awareness and rearm recommendations are a separate optional design comparator. [General transport-airplane design guidance · section 8.d(4), Appendix 2 sections 2.e(3)-(4) and 3.f(3)(a) voice minimum volume](<https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_25.1322-1.pdf>), [DCS F-16CM · pp 41,112 distinguish reset action from voice-system test](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F-16CM · p 157 all-voice message inhibit](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>), [General transport-airplane design guidance · section 8.d and Appendix 2 cancellation/voice-volume guidance](<https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_25.1322-1.pdf>).

**Our captured behavior:** All own pilot-warning voice can be muted or reduced to zero, including urgent terrain speech. The state is exported and visible on the AUDIO page as VOICE OFF/volume, but no persistent forward-field muted indicator was found. The HUD warning text and independent RWR/MWS audio have separate behavior.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The global own-voice inhibit capability agrees with the stated Viper option. The separate chosen general design target for persistent suppression awareness is reduced outside AUDIO. Neither establishes an F-22 mute defect or mandatory critical-message exception.

**Implementation target:** Choose the voice-inhibit/volume policy explicitly. ### VT01 · Probe heating controls and sensor validity are distinct from true icing aerodynamics

**Basis:** F16/Hornet analogue · **Diverges from selected analogue** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P2 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT.

**F-22 evidence boundary:** F-22 climatic testing is public, but the reviewed F-22 sources do not establish a production probe-heater cockpit policy, icing-clearance envelope or accretion curve. The climate laboratory limits are not aircraft certification limits.

**Reference behavior:** DCS Viper provides probe HEAT/TEST with a failed-heater caution; DCS Hornet distinguishes electrically powered ON from airborne AUTO. Generic airframe icing affects lift/drag/thrust/weight, while probe blockage is a separate sensed-air-data problem. [DCS F-16CM · 111](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20F-16C%20Viper%20Guide.pdf>), [DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · 47](<https://assets.chucksguides.com/pdf/DCS%20FA-18C%20Hornet%20Guide.pdf>), [General aircraft weather physics · 7-1-19](<https://www.faa.gov/Air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_1.html>), [F-22 climatic testing · McKinley Climatic Laboratory](<https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/140539/snow-job/>).

**Our captured behavior:** Owned HUD CAS derives from true EFM TAS/sound/pressure with finite-value validity. The atmosphere callback has temperature/density/wind, but no owned ice, moisture/probe-heater state or heater/test control was found. Base input bindings and native host effects remain possible; they were not measured.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The selected explicit heater/test/status workflow is not represented in the owned implementation. This is not proof that DCS provides no rain/icing visuals or that a particular F-22 icing severity must be simulated.

**Implementation target:** Choose an explicitly estimated probe-protection/sensor-failure profile and identify host ownership first. Keep sensed pressure/validity separate from true aerodynamic airflow, and keep airframe/inlet icing effects distinct from probe failure. Adopt qualitative physics without importing another aircraft’s accretion rates or switch labels.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** DCS control-workflow comparison plus general weather physics; total host weather response unresolved.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare declared heater OFF/ON/AUTO and test/fault status with electrical and airborne conditions.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Compare cold dry air, visible moisture and a warm condition without equating low temperature alone with accretion.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Block/fail a sensed probe while retaining true aerodynamic state; restore heating/sensing according to a declared estimate.

**Dependencies:** Weather/host ownership, Probe power/state, Truth-versus-sensor data, Separate inlet/airframe ice scope.

**Re-audit:** New case. VG11 covered generic invalid air-data reversion; this adds weather/probe-heating dependencies and separates sensor ice from airframe/inlet ice.

RAPTOR::ed_fm_get_param has no case for it and returns the default zero; MFD CABINPRESS copies a native cockpit argument. There is no owned source/seal/leak state producing a nonzero increment. The native indication’s meaning has not been measured.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Owned physical export and public system function; exact F-22 curve and host pilot effects unqualified.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** With a declared sealed/pressurized configuration, compare ambient, cabin increment and the resulting indication at several altitudes.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Compare source off, ventilation/dump and a declared leak independently of oxygen product pressure.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Lose/recover sealing or pressure source with finite state response; do not restore pressure merely by clearing a warning.

**Basis:** F22 documented · **Not assessable from available evidence** · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P2 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT.

[F-22A, historical Elmendorf support context · 34](<https://www.saffm.hq.af.mil/Portals/84/documents/FY09/AFD-080204-065.pdf?ver=2016-08-22-141510-773>), [F-22A, historical Elmendorf support context · 26](<https://www.saffm.hq.af.mil/Portals/84/documents/FY08/AFD-070209-046.pdf?ver=2016-08-22-132036-853>), [F-22 climatic testing · McKinley Climatic Laboratory](<https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/140539/snow-job/>).

**Our captured behavior:** APU readiness follows battery reserve, switch/fault state and the same timed ramp at all ambient conditions. Ambient temperature changes the main-engine display envelope but does not enter the APU readiness calculation. No owned cold-soak/preheat state was found.

**Closeness and exact difference:** The current model has no such dependency, but the source cannot locate a valid activation boundary or establish current-era applicability. It would be unjustified to impose a 30-minute wait on every cold start or treat lab chamber limits as start limits.

If adopted, use explicit estimated soak/preheat state and supported ground service, retaining residual warmth. Obtain operating-envelope evidence before claiming an authentic threshold or mandatory wait.

**Applicability / unresolved details:** Historical logistics evidence, not a current flight-manual limit.

**Proposed acceptance — normal:** Compare a sheltered/warm and a declared cold-soaked ground state under the adopted abstraction.

**Proposed acceptance — limits:** Separate ambient temperature, soak duration and residual warmth; do not assume the source supplies their boundaries.

**Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery:** Abort/retry after preheat or partial warm-up without resetting all thermal state or inventing source energy.

**Dependencies:** Declared aircraft era/weather scope, APU readiness, Cold-soak/preheat state, Ground service.
